newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: TransAlta NZ to invest in electricity generation.
newsitem.headline: TransAlta NZ to invest in electricity generation.

text.p: TransAlta New Zealand Ltd, the company formed by the merger of Energy Direct Corp Ltd and unlisted utility Capital Power, said on Monday it was looking to invest in electricity generation in New Zealand.
Energy Direct chief executive Mike Underhill, who will also be chief executive of TransAlta NZ, said the new company will capitalise on the strength of major shareholder TransAlta Corp of Canada.

"TransAlta Holdings is in generation (in Canada). We believe we will probably need to have part of our total supply from our own generation," Underhill told journalists following a special meeting at which shareholders approved the merger.
"The bulk is going to be in wholesale long-term contracts, but we believe it's a sensible portfolio to have some of our own."

Underhill said the new company had not yet devised a timeframe for investment in generation assets, but said TransAlta was interested in any hydro power stations which state-owned Electricity Corp of NZ (ECNZ) may put up for sale.
"The government has said that it is going to sell off some of the ECNZ small hydro schemes. Well, clearly we'd be interested in that."
